scope: Restaurant terrace and lower promenade beside Silcocks, separate from the timber pier deck.
observed: Broad straight stair flight beside the restaurant, divided by handrails; copper/green ornamental column stands on a circular brick plinth beside its foot.
An asphalt access ramp runs beside the staircase from the lower parking/concourse toward the promenade. This ramp is observed, not a proposed patch.

The three apparent low steps in the distant June 2021 view are not established as a separate flight; the closer May 2017 panorama shows a brick plinth. Do not build an invented 20-plus-3 stair arrangement.
Restaurant has an occupied lower frontage below its upper terrace. Existing neutral placeholder has no modelled lower arcade.

ownership.current_defect: The generic south-mainland control grid places upper terrace AND lower concourse at roughly 3.3–3.45m. Lowering only the stair footprint would produce a pit and leave the lower frontage and approaching paths at the upper level.
ownership.required_change: Separate bounded upper terrace, actual ramp, lower concourse and stair footprint. Cut former ground exactly; lower restaurant foundations/arcade ownership must follow the local lower surface. Connect the lower promenade under the pier to the existing marine-lower-promenade level without altering the independent pier deck.

missing_evidence_blocker: A clear view permitting the complete tread count, including the partly hidden first/last tread. Current count is a range, and the earlier supposed extra lower flight was disproved by closer imagery.

A reliable lower-concourse/upper-terrace height difference or one measured riser and verified count. The existing 0.3 m lower control and 3.4 m upper grid are both estimates; their difference is not an independent observation.

A confirmed bounded tie to adjacent lower park/path levels: current coarse ground elsewhere around the concourse also follows the elevated road, so a rectangular low patch would create unsupported cliffs or require invented transition slopes. This must be an explicit local ground-ownership repair, not hidden by a ramp or a detailed raster reconstruction.
